thesis: Owning several businesses preserves ultimate responsibility while making trusted feedback and a life outside work valuable.
summary: The participant rejects an effortless picture of a holding company, saying consequential problems still reach the owner. He describes confronting difficult decisions while maintaining exercise, marriage, friendships, and time with children. Multiple businesses sometimes perform differently at the same time, which he experiences as emotional balance rather than evidence of eliminated financial risk. The discussion closes by distinguishing anonymous criticism from the views of close family and mentors. His stated openness to correction is part of his self-description and is not independently assessed here.
